title: Trump Cracks Jokes (and Insults) at Rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner
summary: Have you ever had a big event get canceled at the last minute? That's what happened to the White House Correspondents' Dinner in April. A gunman caused a scare, so they postponed it. But on Friday night, it was back on—and President Donald Trump was there. Trump spoke for over an hour. He mixed jokes with insults, poking fun at people he doesn't like, from actors to politicians. He even made cracks about their weight and smarts. The audience of journalists laughed at first, but as the jabs kept coming, the room got quieter. He also joked about running for president a third time, which the Constitution doesn't allow. At the end, he put on a red "Trump 2028" hat and pretended to announce a new campaign. "I'm only kidding," he said. Trump said he had toned down his speech from what he planned in April. "That was going to be a doozy," he admitted. He also talked about the awards given to journalists—many for stories critical of him—and asked with a grimace, "Do I have a say in those awards?" The dinner was smaller and tighter on security. Only about 700 people came, and they had to pass through ID checks and sniffing dogs. The head of the correspondents' group, Weijia Jiang, said, "We will not be intimidated. We refuse to let an act of violence have the final word." Trump's return to the dinner was a big moment, especially since he's often attacked the media. But even with jokes, the tension was clear.
why_it_matters: Even leaders and journalists can clash, but traditions like this dinner show that people with different views can still share a room—though sometimes it’s tense.

background_read: The White House Correspondents’ Dinner is a yearly party where reporters and the president joke about the news. It started in 1921 to raise money for journalism scholarships.

Donald Trump skipped the dinner during his first term because he said the media treated him unfairly, so his return this time was a big change. Weijia Jiang is a well-known journalist who leads the White House Correspondents’ Association.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump and journalists at the event
WHAT: Trump gave a long speech mixing jokes with insults at the rescheduled dinner
WHERE: Washington, D.C., at the White House Correspondents' Dinner
WHY: To bring back the tradition after a scare, and Trump used the stage to make fun of his critics and hint at future plans

perspectives.description: They see his jokes as a way to fight back against media that they think treats him unfairly.

They wanted to show they would not be intimidated and that the dinner is about defending free speech.
